project.title: Signal & Story: Data Detective
project.fictionalContext: All organisations, headlines and records in the learner experience are fictional and all datasets are synthetic.
project.provenance: Original synthetic datasets authored for Taskmarket TSK-5DV55M47. They represent invented arcade/puzzle-room records and are not observations of real people or scientific findings.

graphFraming.title: Nova Arcade queue board
graphFraming.construction: Six deliberately simple integer values were chosen to create a modest downward pattern. Changing chart minimum never changes these records or the statistics computed from them.

dictionary.waitSeconds: Synthetic average match wait for that event night, measured in seconds.

sampling.title: Orbit Puzzle Room exit ratings
sampling.construction: The population contains 60 synthetic visits in each time block. Ratings are generated from a repeating deterministic pattern with progressively higher block-level averages, making a closing-hour-only frame visibly unrepresentative of the full population.

dictionary.id: Synthetic visit identifier; not a person identifier.
dictionary.timeBlock: One of four fictional visit windows.
dictionary.rating: Synthetic exit rating on a 1–5 scale.

correlation.title: Skyline Puzzle League sessions
correlation.construction: Forty-five synthetic sessions are split evenly among easy, medium and hard puzzles. Harder groups receive both more hints and longer base completion times. Within a difficulty group, extra hints are constructed to be weakly associated with shorter times, creating a third-variable explanation for the overall positive association.

dictionary.difficulty: Invented puzzle difficulty group: Easy, Medium or Hard.
dictionary.hints: Number of hints used during the synthetic session.
dictionary.seconds: Synthetic puzzle completion time in seconds.

transferCase.headline: FICTIONAL HEADLINE — BrightByte Games: ‘New scoreboard triples replay interest!’
facts: A graph shows replay-interest scores rising from 51 to 55 on a vertical axis drawn from 50 to 56.
The survey link appeared only on the tournament-final screen, even though the claim describes all players.
Players who used the scoreboard more often also tended to play more sessions; session count could help explain both variables.
transferCase.construction: This transfer case is a fictional text-only composite designed to require graph-framing, sampling and correlation reasoning without implying a real product finding.
